title: Human Development: How Age Changes Your Care

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already adjust CPR, the BVM and your words for children and older adults. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Know the age groups and what is normal for each
  2. Why infants and older adults differ inside, and what it changes
  3. Know how age limits your new PCP tools, and the BC head-injury protocol

Textbook: Chapter 9, PDF pages 719–759
slides.say: Welcome back. Today's topic is human development: how body and mind change from birth to old age. As an EMR you already adjust CPR, the bag-valve mask and your words for children and older adults. As a PCP, age matters even more. Many of your new drugs are dosed by weight and limited by age, and your fluid decisions depend on how much reserve the patient has. Today we cover three things: the age groups and what's normal for each, why infants and older adults are different inside, and how age limits your new tools, including the BC head-injury protocol.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。今天的主题是人的生长发育：身体和心理从出生到老年怎样变化。作为 EMR，你已经会针对儿童和老人调整 CPR、球囊面罩和说话方式。作为 PCP，年龄更加重要：你的很多新药按体重给药、受年龄限制，补液决定也取决于病人有多少储备。今天讲三件事：各年龄段的划分和各自的正常值；婴儿和老人身体内部为什么不同；年龄怎样限制你的新工具，包括 BC 的颅脑外伤流程。

slides.title: The age groups
slides.body:
GroupAge
Neonatebirth – 1 month
Infant1 month – 1 year
Toddler1 – 2 years
Preschooler3 – 5 years
School-age6 – 12 years
Adolescent13 – 18 years
Early adult19 – 40 years
Middle adult41 – 60 years
Late adult61 years and older

The younger the patient, the faster the pulse and breathing.
slides.say: First, the names, because they come up on exams and in your reports. A neonate is from birth to one month. An infant is one month to one year. A toddler is one to two, a preschooler three to five, a school-age child six to twelve, and an adolescent thirteen to eighteen. Early adults are nineteen to forty, middle adults forty-one to sixty, and late adults sixty-one and older. One rule for children: the younger the patient, the faster the heart rate and the breathing. Keep that in mind before you call a small child's vital signs abnormal.
slides.sayZh: 先记名称，因为考试和报告里都会用到。新生儿是出生到一个月；婴儿是一个月到一岁；学步期是一到两岁，学龄前是三到五岁，学龄儿童是六到十二岁，青少年是十三到十八岁。成年早期是十九到四十岁，中年是四十一到六十岁，老年是六十一岁及以上。儿童有一条规律：年龄越小，心率和呼吸越快。在判定小孩生命体征异常之前，先记住这一点。

slides.title: Infants: vital signs and weight
slides.body:
• At birth: pulse ≈ 140, breathing 30–60/min
  • Systolic: 67–84 at birth → 85–104 by age 1
  • Tidal volume 6–8 mL/kg → 10–15 mL/kg by age 1; SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Birth ≈ 3.4 kg; loses 5–10% in week 1; ×2 by 6 months, ×3 by 1 year
  • Book: newborn glucose ≥ 45 mg/dL, ≥ 60 mg/dL from 1 month
  • BC: low glucose = BGL < 4.0 mmol/L at every age
slides.say: At birth, the average pulse is about one hundred forty, and breathing is thirty to sixty a minute. Systolic pressure is sixty-seven to eighty-four at birth, and eighty-five to one hundred four by age one. A term baby weighs about three point four kilograms, loses five to ten percent in the first week, then doubles that weight by six months and triples it by one year. Why does weight matter to a PCP? Because your fluid bolus and many child doses are per kilogram. And for the exam: the book gives special newborn glucose limits, but BC treats a glucose under four point zero as low at every age.
slides.sayZh: 出生时平均心率约一百四十，呼吸每分钟三十到六十次。收缩压出生时六十七到八十四，一岁时八十五到一百零四。足月儿出生约三点四公斤，第一周体重下降百分之五到十，之后六个月翻倍，一岁时是出生体重的三倍。体重对 PCP 为什么重要？因为你的推注补液和很多儿童剂量都按公斤算。还有一个考点：书里给了新生儿专用的血糖下限，但 BC 规定各年龄一律以血糖低于四点零为低血糖。

slides.title: The infant airway and breathing
slides.body:
• Mostly nose breathers for months; a blocked nose = trouble
  • Diaphragm does the work → count breaths at the belly
  • Big tongue, short narrow airway → blocks easily
  • Small oxygen reserve, fast oxygen use → fails quickly
  • Weak accessory muscles → tire early

Heavy head: infants often land head first → check head, neck and spine.
slides.say: An infant's airway is not just a small adult airway. For the first months, infants breathe mostly through the nose, and under six months they get blocked noses easily, which can look like choking. Their ribs are soft and the diaphragm does most of the work, so count breaths by watching the belly. The tongue is large and the airway short and narrow, so it blocks easily. They have a small oxygen reserve and use oxygen fast, so they slide into respiratory failure quickly, and their accessory muscles tire early. And because the head is heavy, infants often land head first when they fall.
slides.sayZh: 婴儿的气道不只是缩小版的成人气道。出生后几个月，婴儿主要用鼻子呼吸，六个月以下特别容易鼻塞，看起来就像噎住了。他们的肋骨软，主要靠膈肌呼吸，所以数呼吸要看肚子的起伏。舌头相对大，气道又短又窄，很容易堵。他们的氧储备小、耗氧快，所以很快就会滑向呼吸衰竭，辅助呼吸肌也很早就累了。另外头比较重，婴儿摔倒时常常头先着地。

slides.q: A mother says her 2-month-old "keeps choking" and is working hard to breathe. No fever, no known foreign body. What should you check early, specific to this age?
options: Whether the nose is blocked with mucus
The capillary refill on the forehead
The grip strength in both hands
slides.say: Quick question. A mother says her two-month-old keeps choking and is working hard to breathe. There's no fever and no known foreign body. What should you check early, specific to this age? A, whether the nose is blocked with mucus. B, the capillary refill on the forehead. C, whether the fontanelle has closed. D, the grip strength in both hands. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 小测验。一位母亲说她两个月大的宝宝老是噎住，呼吸很费力。没有发热，也没有已知异物。针对这个月龄，你应该先查什么？A，鼻子是不是被黏液堵住了；B，额头的毛细血管再充盈；C，囟门是否已经闭合；D，双手的握力。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is A. Young infants breathe mainly through the nose, so mucus can block their airflow and look like choking, and clearing the nose may solve the problem. B tells you about perfusion, not the cause of hard breathing. C is wrong; fontanelles normally stay open until about age two, and the anterior fontanelle helps you judge hydration, not this airway problem. D tests the palmar grasp reflex, not the airway.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 A。小婴儿主要用鼻子呼吸，黏液会挡住气流、看起来像噎住，把鼻子清理干净可能就解决了。B 反映的是灌注，不是呼吸费力的原因；C 错，囟门一般到两岁左右才闭合，前囟帮你判断脱水，与这个气道问题无关；D 测的是掌握反射，不是气道。

slides.title: Infants: fluids, fontanelles, reflexes
slides.body:
• Kidneys can't concentrate urine → dehydrate fast
  • Sunken anterior fontanelle → think dehydration
  • Fontanelles close by about age 2
  • Some of mother's immunity lasts about the first year
  • Reflexes: Moro (startle), palmar grasp, rooting, sucking
  • Poor temperature control → keep them covered
slides.say: Infant kidneys can't concentrate urine well, so when an infant loses fluid from vomiting or diarrhea, they dry out faster and compensate less than an adult. A useful sign is the anterior fontanelle, the soft spot on top of the head: if it's sunken, think dehydration. The fontanelles close by about age two. Infants keep some of their mother's antibodies for about the first year, which is passive immunity. You'll also see newborn reflexes: the startle or Moro reflex, the palmar grasp, rooting toward a touch on the cheek, and sucking. And infants control their temperature poorly, so keep them covered while you assess.
slides.sayZh: 婴儿的肾脏浓缩尿液的能力差，所以呕吐或腹泻丢液时，他们比成人脱水更快、代偿更差。一个有用的体征是前囟，也就是头顶的软点：如果凹陷，要想到脱水。囟门约两岁闭合。婴儿在出生后第一年左右保有母亲的部分抗体，这是被动免疫。你还会看到新生儿反射：受惊时的拥抱反射，也叫 Moro 反射；掌握反射；碰脸颊就转头的觅食反射；以及吸吮反射。另外婴儿体温调节差，评估时要给他们盖好。

slides.title: Toddlers to school age
slides.body:
• Toddler 1–2, preschooler 3–5: systolic ≈ 100
  • Weak breathing muscles: can't keep up fast, deep breathing for long
  • Mother's antibodies fade → frequent colds
  • Keep routines, family and a favourite toy close
  • Show on a toy before you do it
  • School age 6–12: near-adult vitals; +2.5–3.5 kg and 5–6 cm a year
slides.say: Toddlers and preschoolers have slower vital signs than infants, with a systolic around one hundred. Their lungs keep growing, but their breathing muscles are still weak, so they can't keep up fast, deep breathing for long. A child who has been working hard and suddenly slows down may be tiring out, not getting better. They also lose their mother's antibodies and catch colds often. To communicate, keep family and a favourite toy close, and show what you'll do before you do it, for example by putting the blood pressure cuff on a stuffed animal first. From six to twelve, school-age children have nearly adult vital signs.
slides.sayZh: 学步期和学龄前儿童的生命体征比婴儿慢，收缩压约一百。他们的肺还在发育，但呼吸肌仍然弱，没法长时间维持又快又深的呼吸。一个一直很费力呼吸的孩子突然慢下来，可能是累垮了，而不是好转。他们也失去了来自母亲的抗体，经常感冒。沟通时，让家人和心爱的玩具留在身边，做之前先演示，比如先把血压袖带绑在毛绒玩具上。六到十二岁的学龄儿童，生命体征已接近成人。

slides.title: Adolescents: adult body, teen mind
slides.body:
• 13–18: systolic 110–131, pulse 60–100, breathing 12–20
  • Growth spurt: girls usually earlier than boys
  • Want privacy and control; fear embarrassment
  • Higher risk of depression and suicide

Ask sensitive questions in private. With family present, teens may not tell the whole truth.
slides.say: Adolescents are thirteen to eighteen. Their vital signs settle into adult ranges: a systolic of about one hundred ten to one hundred thirty-one, a pulse of sixty to one hundred, and breathing twelve to twenty. Girls usually hit their growth spurt earlier than boys. Emotionally, teens want privacy and control, they're building an identity, and they're often terrified of being embarrassed. They also have a higher risk of depression and suicide. The practical lesson: with parents in the room, a teenager may not tell you the whole truth about sex, drugs or alcohol. Find a private moment to ask those questions, and document what you learn.
slides.sayZh: 青少年是十三到十八岁。他们的生命体征进入成人范围：收缩压约一百一十到一百三十一，脉搏六十到一百，呼吸十二到二十。女孩的生长突增通常比男孩早。心理上，青少年想要隐私和自主，正在建立自我认同，而且常常非常怕丢脸。他们抑郁和自杀的风险也更高。实用的一课：父母在场时，青少年可能不会把性、毒品或酒精的实情全告诉你。找个私下的机会问这些问题，并把了解到的情况记录下来。

slides.title: Adults: the long middle
slides.body:
Early adult19–40; peak 19 to mid-20spulse ≈ 70, BP ≈ 120/80
Middle adult41–60; heart disease, cancervision, hearing, menopause
Sarcopeniamuscle loss ≈ 1% a yearup to 50% by the 80s–90s

Health varies widely in middle age: assess the person, not the number.
slides.say: Early adults are nineteen to forty. The body works at its best from nineteen to the mid-twenties, with a pulse around seventy and a blood pressure around one hundred twenty over eighty. From middle age, people lose about one percent of their muscle mass a year, and in severe cases about half by their eighties or nineties. This is sarcopenia, and exercise can slow it. Middle adults, forty-one to sixty, see more heart disease and cancer, and changes in vision and hearing; menopause usually comes in the late forties or early fifties. Health varies widely at this age, so assess the person, not the number.
slides.sayZh: 成年早期是十九到四十岁。身体机能在十九岁到二十五六岁最好，脉搏约七十，血压约一百二十比八十。从中年起，人每年流失约百分之一的肌肉，严重者到八九十岁会丢掉约一半，这叫肌少症，运动可以延缓。中年人，四十一到六十岁，心脏病和癌症增多，视力和听力也会变化；绝经通常在四十多岁末到五十出头。这个年龄段健康状况差异很大，所以要评估这个人，而不是看年龄数字。

slides.title: Older adults: less reserve everywhere
slides.body:
• Stiff vessels (elasticity down up to 70%) → poor BP compensation
  • Heart can't raise its output much on demand
  • Weak cough and gag → aspiration risk
  • Vital capacity ↓, residual volume ↑ → CO₂ can build up at rest
  • Kidneys cope poorly with fluid and electrolyte stress
  • Often many medications
slides.say: Late adults, sixty-one and older, have less reserve everywhere. Blood vessels lose up to seventy percent of their elasticity, so the body can't adjust blood pressure well, and the heart can't raise its output much when it's needed. So an older patient can be in serious trouble with vital signs that don't look alarming. The cough and gag reflexes weaken, which makes aspiration more likely. Less air moves in and out and more stays trapped, so carbon dioxide can build up even at rest. The kidneys cope poorly with fluid and electrolyte stress, so give fluid in steps and listen to the lungs.
slides.sayZh: 六十一岁及以上的老年人，各方面储备都少。血管弹性最多丢失百分之七十，身体调节血压的能力差；心脏在需要时也提高不了多少输出量。所以老人可能已经很危险，生命体征看起来却不吓人。咳嗽和呕吐反射减弱，更容易误吸。进出的气体变少、滞留的变多，所以即使在静息时二氧化碳也可能潴留。肾脏应对体液和电解质波动的能力差，所以补液要分步给、边补边听肺。

slides.title: Older adults: brain and senses
slides.body:
• Brain shrinks 10–20% by age 80
  • Gap under the dura stretches the bridging veins
  • Minor bump → slow subdural bleed; signs appear late
  • Feels heat, cold and sharp things less → more injuries
  • Hearing loss ≈ 4× more common than vision loss; high tones go first
slides.say: The brain also shrinks, by ten to twenty percent by age eighty. That leaves a gap between the brain and the dura, its tough outer covering, and stretches the bridging veins that cross the gap. A fall or a bump can tear them. Blood slowly fills the gap, and the pressure inside the skull doesn't rise until the space is full, so the signs of a subdural hematoma can appear late. A well-looking older patient after a head bump is not cleared. And hearing loss is about four times more common than vision loss, with high tones lost first, so face the patient and speak clearly in a lower voice.
slides.sayZh: 大脑也会萎缩，到八十岁时缩小百分之十到二十。这样大脑和硬脑膜之间就出现了空隙，横跨空隙的桥静脉被拉长，摔一跤或磕一下就可能撕裂。血慢慢填满空隙，在空隙填满之前颅内压不会升高，所以硬膜下血肿的征象可能很晚才出现。老人磕了头、看起来没事，不等于排除了问题。另外听力下降比视力下降常见约四倍，高音先丢失，所以要面对病人，用较低的声音清楚地说话。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: BC brain injury protocol
slides.body:
Head trauma + any altered LOC → suspect TBI. GCS ≥ 13 mild · 9–12 moderate · ≤ 8 severe

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Oxygen to keep SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if breathing is failing
  • Head of the bed up 30°
  • Loosen the hard collar

PCP adds

  • Keep glucose 4.0–8.0 mmol/L
  • Keep systolic > 120 mmHg
  • IV to keep the vein open (TKVO) if systolic > 120
  • No TXA for an isolated TBI
slides.say: Here's the BC protocol for traumatic brain injury. Suspect a brain injury in anyone with head trauma and any change in level of consciousness. A GCS of thirteen or more is mild, nine to twelve moderate, and eight or less severe. For all licence levels: oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four or higher, assisted breaths if breathing is failing, the head of the bed up thirty degrees, and a loosened hard collar. The PCP adds: keep the glucose between four and eight, keep the systolic above one hundred twenty, and run the IV just to keep the vein open when it's above one hundred twenty. And no TXA for an isolated brain injury.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的颅脑外伤流程。凡是头部外伤并有任何意识水平改变的，都要怀疑颅脑外伤。GCS 十三分及以上为轻度，九到十二为中度，八分及以下为重度。所有执照级别都做的：给氧使血氧保持在九十四以上；呼吸衰竭时辅助通气；床头抬高三十度；松开硬颈托。PCP 多做的：血糖维持在四到八之间，收缩压维持在一百二十以上，收缩压高于一百二十时静脉只以保持通畅的速度滴注。另外，单纯颅脑外伤不给 TXA。

slides.q: An 84-year-old fell and bumped her head 2 hours ago. She is alert, GCS 15, vital signs normal, and wants to stay home. What is the best approach?
options: Normal findings rule out a brain bleed; she can stay home
A bleed may not show yet; encourage transport and reassess often
Give TXA, because she is within 3 hours of the injury
Lay her flat with a tight collar to protect the spine
slides.say: Last question. An eighty-four-year-old woman fell and bumped her head two hours ago. She's alert, her GCS is fifteen, her vital signs are normal, and she wants to stay home. What is the best approach? A, normal findings rule out a brain bleed, so she can stay home. B, a bleed may not show yet, so encourage transport and reassess often. C, give TXA, because she is within three hours of the injury. D, lay her flat with a tight collar to protect the spine. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 最后一题。一位八十四岁的女士两小时前摔倒磕到头。她神志清楚，GCS 十五分，生命体征正常，想留在家里。最好的做法是什么？A，检查正常就排除了颅内出血，她可以留在家里；B，出血可能还没表现出来，劝她去医院并频繁复评；C，给 TXA，因为受伤还不到三小时；D，让她平躺、戴紧颈托保护脊柱。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. In older adults, a slow subdural bleed can fill the space left by brain shrinkage before the pressure rises, so early findings can be falsely reassuring. A is the trap. C is wrong; in BC, TXA is contraindicated for an isolated brain injury. D is wrong; the BC brain injury protocol raises the head of the bed thirty degrees and loosens the hard collar.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。老人大脑萎缩留下空隙，缓慢的硬膜下出血可以先把空隙填满，颅内压才升高，所以早期检查结果可能给人虚假的安心。A 就是陷阱；C 错，在 BC，单纯颅脑外伤是 TXA 的禁忌；D 错，BC 颅脑外伤流程要求床头抬高三十度并松开硬颈托。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: age limits
slides.body:
• CPAP: only age 13 and over
  • TXA: never under age 12
  • Dexamethasone, child: 0.5 mg/kg, max 16 mg; by mouth preferred
  • Ondansetron: 2 mg at 6 months–4 years; 4 mg from age 4
  • Diphenhydramine: not for newborns
  • Ipratropium: not under 30 days; child neb 250 mcg
slides.say: As a PCP, your new tools come with age rules you never needed as an EMR. CPAP is only for patients aged thirteen and over. TXA is never given under age twelve. Dexamethasone for a child is zero point five milligrams per kilogram, up to sixteen milligrams, preferably by mouth. Ondansetron is two milligrams from six months to four years, and four milligrams from age four. Diphenhydramine is not for newborns, and ipratropium is not for babies under thirty days; the child nebulizer dose is two hundred fifty micrograms. Many child doses are per kilogram, so estimate the weight carefully, and check the age limit before you draw up the drug.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，你的新工具附带着当 EMR 时用不到的年龄规定。CPAP 只用于十三岁及以上。TXA 绝不用于十二岁以下。儿童地塞米松每公斤零点五毫克，最多十六毫克，首选口服。昂丹司琼六个月到四岁给两毫克，四岁起给四毫克。苯海拉明不用于新生儿；异丙托溴铵不用于未满三十天的婴儿，儿童雾化剂量是二百五十微克。很多儿童剂量按公斤计算，所以要仔细估计体重，抽药之前先核对年龄限制。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Younger = faster pulse and breathing; infants block, tire and dry out fast
  2. Older adults: little reserve; a head bump can bleed late — TBI: systolic > 120, glucose 4–8
  3. Age limits your tools: CPAP ≥ 13, no TXA < 12, many doses per kg

Next: Chapter 10, Patient Communication
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: the younger the patient, the faster the pulse and breathing, and infants block their airways, tire and dry out quickly. Two: older adults have little reserve, and a simple head bump can bleed late. For a brain injury, the PCP keeps the systolic above one hundred twenty and the glucose between four and eight. Three: age limits your new tools: CPAP from thirteen, no TXA under twelve, and many doses by weight. Next is Chapter 10, patient communication, which builds on how you talk to each age group. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，年龄越小，脉搏和呼吸越快；婴儿气道容易堵、容易累、容易脱水。二，老人储备少，简单磕一下头也可能迟发出血；颅脑外伤时 PCP 要把收缩压维持在一百二十以上、血糖在四到八之间。三，年龄限制你的新工具：CPAP 十三岁起，十二岁以下不给 TXA，很多剂量按体重算。下一章是第十章「与病人沟通」，会在你今天学到的各年龄段沟通方式上继续展开。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
